long_biography.plain_text:
Restoring historic hotels was a priority for Sheikh Nawaf bin Jassim bin Jabor Al Thani at Katara Hospitality. At the reopening of Lausanne’s Royal Savoy, he described the renewal of historic buildings as central to the company’s approach. The hotel retained its period character while adding contemporary facilities.

His charitable work included chairing the Jassim and Hamad bin Jassim Charitable Foundation, which finances projects through property and financial investments. He promoted programmes intended to make communities more self-reliant. The foundation’s industrial training institute in Maharashtra produced graduates who entered jobs in their own region.

confidence.reason: The hotel group's direct reopening release supports restoration strategy and renewed facilities. The charity's twentieth-anniversary report identifies his chairmanship, developmental approach, investment funding and the vocational graduates entering local employment. It does not attribute foundation money to him personally.
